pr_title: Bluetooth: Convert HCI drivers to use a proper Zephyr driver API
pr_body:
Current status:

- [x] Create a base binding and API definition
- [x] Update the host to support new HCI driver instances
- [x] Update `h4.c`
- [x] Update native controller HCI driver
- [x] Fix `samples/bluetooth/hci_uart_async/` to work with the new driver model
- [x] Fix bsim to work both with native and UART-based controllers (right now CI is failing)
- [x] Figure out what to do with `bt_read_static_addr()`. Taken care of by #72580
- [x] Figure out what to do with `BT_HAS_HCI_VS`, `BT_HCI_VS` and `BT_HCI_VS_EXT` (perhaps DTS properties?). Some preparation in #72580.
- [x] Fix controller unit tests: no devicetree available for `unit_testing` "board" right now: #72871
- [x] Update `ipc.c`
- [x] Update `userchan.c`
- [x] Update `h5.c`
- [x] Update `hci_ambiq.c` (and associated DT binding)
- [x] Remove `hci_b91.c`: #73289
- [x] Update `hci_esp32.c`
- [x] Update `hci_psoc6_bless.c` (and associated DT binding)
- [x] Update `hci_spi_st.c` (and associated DT binding)
- [x] Update `hci_stm32wba.c`
- [x] Update `ipm_stm32wb.c` (and associated DT binding)
- [x] Update `spi.c`
- [x] Update `hci_da1469x.c`
- [x] Update `hci_nxp.c`
- [x] Update `slz_hci.c`
- [x] Update documentation, especially stuff regarding `/chosen` properties
- [x] Make it possible for `nrf52_bsim` to use also UART for HCI
- [x] Update various apps under `samples/` and `tests/` that use the legacy HCI driver API
- [x] Get rid of the Kconfig `choice` section for HCI drivers
- [x] Get rid of `BT_NO_DRIVER`
- [x] Deprecate the old API
- [ ] Lots of testing
  - [x] bsim with virtual driver (hci_driver.c)
  - [x] ipc.c tested in CI
  - [ ] Test on hardware with virtual bus (i.e. combined build)
  - [ ]  Test on hardware with IPC (i.e. split build)
  - [ ]  Test on hardware with UART (i.e. split build)
  - [x]  userchan.c
  - [ ] Test with an OoT driver (e.g. NCS)

Right now the host `hci_core.c` uses `#if DT_HAS_CHOSEN(zephyr_bt_hci)` to separate the new-style HCI drivers from the legacy HCI driver support. The old API has been deprecated, but will only be removed after a deprecation period.

The following drivers depend on "west blobs", so they're not covered by CI, but were manually compile tested:

- `hci_psoc6_bless.c` (`west blobs fetch hal_infineon`)
- `hci_esp32.c` (`west blobs fetch hal_espressif`)
- `hci_stm32wba.c` (`west blobs fetch hal_stm32` doesn't work for me, see https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/72323#issuecomment-2143443846 )
- `slz_hci.c` (`west blobs fetch hal_silabs`, same problem for me as with stm32, i.e. had to manually download)

What this PR *doesn't* try to tackle:

- Find a solution for and fix driver dependencies on host HCI command sending APIs, which are e.g. not available with HCI_RAW. https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/d3c0dfbf3699fc98e01909ecf9a2ee834d7f4d41/drivers/bluetooth/hci/apollox_blue.c#L289-L333
- Decide what to do with `BT_HCI_ACL_FLOW_CONTROL` currently referencing specific HCI drivers
- net_buf allocations by drivers. Drivers should own their own memory rather than calling into the host side to do these allocations.
- Making the HCI driver API support system calls. This is related to the above first point. We also can't have the driver make direct calls using the `recv` callback to the host, rather there needs to be another mechanism for the host to fetch data from the driver.

Fixes #51503
pr_comments: @jhedberg May I know what the main issue will be addressed by this driver API converting? It seems the changes are wide so I would like to know more about the background and see what comments I can give for HCI Ambiq codes. Thanks.

> @jhedberg May I know what the main issue will be addressed by this driver API converting? It seems the changes are wide so I would like to know more about the background and see what comments I can give for HCI Ambiq codes. Thanks.

@aaronyegx most of the justifications can be found in the linked issue, i.e. #51503. Additionally, longer term we're considering the possibility of having the Bluetooth host run in user space. The primary way for user space to communicate with kernel space is through the system call interface, and there's a well established way how to do this for Zephyr driver APIs. Note that this aspect is something that's going to happen much later in the future (if at all) - the justifications in #51503 should be sufficient in themselves.

@aaronyegx I've pushed a conversion commit for the Ambiq HCI driver (https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/72323/commits/f15a7bf78243f7eb4f11a8f5767fa4df47ccc767). It's a very simplistic one which doesn't e.g. try to add support for multiple instances (i.e. I keep the global variables instead of moving them to the instance structs). Could you take a look? I was able to verify that it builds, but I have no idea if it still works on actual HW.

> Should we update infineon,cyw43xxx-bt-hci binding or board dtsi to addition enable zephyr,bt-hci-uart as well.

@npal-cy thanks for discovering this issue. It seems I overlooked the various extensions to the standard drivers, like `h4.c` (basically I thought the extensions wouldn't be drivers in themselves, having their own DT_DRV_COMPAT, etc). The `h4.c` driver gets enabled by having a `zephyr,bt-hci-uart` DTS node, so I think that can't be avoided. The way I'd structure this, is to place the `zephyr,bt-hci-uart` node as a child of the actual UART node (like I've done in other places in this PR), and then the `infineon,cyw43xxx-bt-hci` node would be a child of that one. That way you could just reference `DT_GPARENT()` from the cyw43xxx driver instead of relying on `DT_CHOSEN(zephyr_bt_uart)` (a property which should really go away as part of this PR). Does that sound alright?

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: HCI drivers should be first-class Zephyr drivers (driver API, DTS, etc)
comments:
Hi @jori-nordic, @jhedberg,

This issue, marked as an Enhancement, was opened a while ago and did not get any traction. It was just assigned to you based on the labels. If you don't consider yourself the right person to address this issue, please re-assing it to the right person.

Please take a moment to review if the issue is still relevant to the project.  If it is, please provide feedback and direction on how to move forward. If it is not, has already been addressed, is a duplicate, or is no longer relevant, please close it with a short comment explaining the reason.

@jhedberg you are also encouraged to help moving this issue forward by providing additional information and confirming this request/issue is still relevant to you.

Thanks!

review_comments: Is there a reason for leaving the transport setup and teardown out of the driver API? It looks like these will always used together with `open` and `close`. Maybe we should utilize the setup API to pass in the HCI transport device to be used in `open` and `close`?

This is really just something inherited from the original `include/drivers/bluetooth/hci_driver.h`. This API should probably be moved somewhere else since it's really an extension that some drivers have chosen but it's not really part of the generic HCI driver API (that the host or `hci_raw.c` see).
Minor suggestion: Move the definition of `setup` before `open` to make it clear that `setup` will always be called before `open`.

> Minor suggestion: Move the definition of `setup` before `open` to make it clear that `setup` will always be called before `open`.

It's actually the other way around. `setup()` is intended for driver-related HCI commands (often vendor ones) which should be sent before the host starts sending any HCI commands. The HCI transport is not considered to be open before `open()` has returned successfully, which is why the separate `setup()` callback exists.

I think what causes confusion is that some drivers (`h4.c` and `ipc.c` in particular) have chosen `bt_hci_transport_setup()` as the name for a `__weak` function that can be used for low-level initialization of the transport (not related to actual HCI communication).

This is not particularly clean, however I didn't immediately see a way to get the `const struct device *` routed to the `sink_sdu_emit_hci()` call. In all the other cases (e.g. the rx threads) I was able to pass the `struct device` as a callback parameter.

How do we envision that this API is extended for future use cases?
Right now it is only used to set public address, but later it may be used to configure power mode or something else.
Will there be cases where some parameters are used by some vendors only?

As the API definition and driver code are located in the same place we know that these will always be in sync, so it may not be a big issue. If there is something vendor specific we can hide it behind KConfig options

> How do we envision that this API is extended for future use cases?
> Right now it is only used to set public address, but later it may be used to configure power mode or something else.
> Will there be cases where some parameters are used by some vendors only?

All good questions. The parameter is in the form of a struct in order to provide some more flexibility and easier extension in the future. I don't see how this could contain vendor-specific extensions though, since our host-side code is (at least right now) rather vendor agnostic.

In general, discussing future of this API is something we should certainly do, but I feel that it's out of scope of this PR. The size of this PR is already quite large as-is, so I've tried to keep the semantics as close to 1:1 to the old API as possible, and leave any further API redesign for later.

It is not clear to me whether this API is experimental, stable or unstable. 
Suggest to add a version to it as per https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/develop/api/overview.html#api-overview to indicate it's mature-ness

> It is not clear to me whether this API is experimental, stable or unstable. Suggest to add a version to it as per https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/develop/api/overview.html#api-overview to indicate it's mature-ness

@carlescufi can you help out here? I think probably "unstable" is the right categorization. It can't be experimental at least, since we couldn't deprecate the old API otherwise.
Definitely "unstable", correct, no other definition fits this specific usecase. This API is new but already has multiple implementations and is the successor to an established one.
Do you remember the reason for reordering statements in `bt_disable()`?

> Do you remember the reason for reordering statements in `bt_disable()`?

Yes. There were actions in `bt_disable()` that triggered HCI activity, so calling `close()` had to be moved after those.
